reasoning: Set A takes the project all the way to the point where building can start. It has seven milestones with Outlines and checkable Exits. M1 is a walking skeleton across eqdata, server and web, and its plan opens with a Phase 0 interface task (M1-T01) that freezes the contracts and fixture-backed fakes. Spines follow, then thicken, wiring and system tasks, with a dependency graph whose edges and `none:` reasons I checked and found valid. The todo starts at M1-T01, and the packets carry the frozen types, golden cases and acceptance checks a builder needs. The references are summarised correctly, with their caveats carried into the design (per-window fit), and assigned to M4/M5 (RF-01) and M6 (RF-02/03). Its weaknesses: it splits the user's Stage 4 into two stages (S4 forecasts, S5 agents), the plan keeps process narration (Replan notes, an open question saying 'dataviz isn't installed'), some step tags don't line up, and the docs are heavy. Set B's design is sound: architecture, AD decisions, a harness whose `decide` step uses the null-hypothesis-testing skill, a per-window RF-01 adaptation, and clear pipelines such as PL-17 and PL-18. But it stops before the build. There are no milestones in the roadmap, and no tasks/plan.md, todo.md, CONSTRAINTS.md, AGENTS.md or context packets. So milestone quality, dependency graph, interface freeze, task buildability and finding the next build step all fail. Its S2 Skills line also leaves out null-hypothesis-testing, even though PL-17's `decide` step uses that skill.

strengths: Complete chain from roadmap to milestones to M1 plan, todo and per-task packets
Phase 0 interface task freezes the contracts, with fixture-backed fakes and a mock server
Point-in-time design (bitemporal store, AD-07 query-time returns) with closed-form golden cases
References correctly summarised, caveats carried into the design, assigned to the right milestones
Each later milestone's Depends cell names the exact symbols it consumes
weaknesses: Splits the user's Stage 4 into S4 and S5
Plan keeps Replan notes and process narration
Very verbose (explained docs, long Read lists)
M1-T01 is a large cross-package freeze in one task

strengths: Clear architecture with enforced import directions and torch isolated in `learn`
Shared registration/guarded-view harness, with Holm correction and per-candidate verdicts
Readable PL-17/PL-18 step tables, entry sketches and planned layout
RF-01's look-ahead turned into a per-window fit with out-of-sample loadings

weaknesses: No milestones, plan, todo, CONSTRAINTS, AGENTS or context packets: building can't start
Roadmap Status 'Specced' for every stage, with no Exit criteria
S2 Skills line leaves out null-hypothesis-testing even though PL-17's `decide` step uses it
Process narration in architecture ('The probe answers before `pipeline-design` starts')
